## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

- **Title**: gh-1061 Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1061` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +336
- **Deletions**: -24

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:52:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.
- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.
- `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` + `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`: added the AC5 sentence — ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md`, even when blocked; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

### Notes
- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

The repo's CRAP threshold is 8 and the ratchet only allows pre-baseline offenders; every function introduced by this PR must land at ≤ 8. The established remediation pattern is in recent history (gh-1036–gh-1039 are all `[CRAP]` split PRs): extract helpers until each new function drops under the threshold.

Suggested split for `threadShortLabel` — extract the id-resolution and body-snippet steps:

```javascript
function shortThreadId(t) {
    var id = t.threadId ||
        (t.rootCommentId !== null && t.rootCommentId !== undefined ? 'comment#' + t.rootCommentId : 'no-id');
    id = String(id);
    return id.length > 16 ? id.substring(0, 13) + '...' : id;
}

function capLen(s, cap) {
    return s.length > cap ? s.substring(0, cap - 3) + '...' : s;
}

function threadShortLabel(t, maxLen) {
    if (!t) return '(unknown thread)';
    var body = String(t.body || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
    return capLen(shortThreadId(t) + (body ? ' — "' + body + '"' : ''), maxLen || 40);
}
```

`runCase` (14.1) and the inline `file_read` mock (11.1) in `test_pushReworkChanges.js` need the same treatment — e.g. extract the `cli_execute_command` git-stub and the `file_read` path-dispatch into named suite-level helpers. CI will not go green until all three are ≤ 8.

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):

`buildReplyCoverage` now returns `totalOpenCount: open.length`, but no production caller reads it — the only reference is the new unit test asserting its value. The gate now runs on `replyCoverage.openCount` (addressable only, gh-1061 AC3), but the blocked path still passes `openInputThreads.length` (ALL open threads, null-id machine notices included) into `handleReworkBlocked`. **dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `isUnaddressableThread` is evaluated twice per open thread**

`buildReplyCoverage` computes the unaddressable set with one `filter(isUnaddressableThread)` pass and then the addressable set with a second, negated `filter`. `threadKeyOf()` is cheap so this is not a performance issue, but the two filters are one classification viewed twice — a single pass building both buckets (or deriving `addressable = open` minus the unaddressable set) would be clearer and cannot drift if the predicate ever becomes more expensive. }# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):

The Quality workflow's `crap` check fails on this PR (run 39159678077, exit code 2; the log was fetched via dmtools since `ci_failures_full.log` could not be retrieved):

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/pushReworkChanges.js::threadShortLabel: 10.5
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js::runCase: 14.1
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js::file_read#20: 11.1
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 3 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The repo's CRAP threshold is 8 and the ratchet only allows pre-baseline offenders; every function introduced by this PR must land at ≤ 8. The established remediation pattern is in recent history (gh-1036–gh-1039 are all `[CRAP]` split PRs): extract helpers until each new function drops under the threshold.

Suggested split for `threadShortLabel` — extract the id-resolution and body-snippet steps:

```javascript
function shortThreadId(t) {
    var id = t.threadId ||
        (t.rootCommentId !== null && t.rootCommentId !== undefined ? 'comment#' + t.rootCommentId : 'no-id');
    id = String(id);
    return id.length > 16 ? id.substring(0, 13) + '...' : id;
}

function capLen(s, cap) {
    return s.length > cap ? s.substring(0, cap - 3) + '...' : s;
}

function threadShortLabel(t, maxLen) {
    if (!t) return '(unknown thread)';
    var body = String(t.body || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
    return capLen(shortThreadId(t) + (body ? ' — "' + body + '"' : ''), maxLen || 40);
}
```

`runCase` (14.1) and the inline `file_read` mock (11.1) in `test_pushReworkChanges.js` need the same treatment — e.g. extract the `cli_execute_command` git-stub and the `file_read` path-dispatch into named suite-level helpers. CI will not go green until all three are ≤ 8.

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.

- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.
- `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` + `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`: added the AC5 sentence — ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md`, even when blocked; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

content.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)
        # Dynamic shields.io endpoint badges: the numbers come from this run, the JSON lives on an
        # orphan 'badges' branch, so nothing in the code tree changes (no PR conflicts, no bot
        # commits on main). Cosmetic — never fails the pipeline.
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          node - <<'JS'
          const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
          const tmp = process.env.RUNNER_TEMP, thr = Number(process.env.CRAP_THRESHOLD);
          const cov = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'cov/coverage-final.json'), 'utf8'));
          let t = 0, h = 0;
          for (const [f, e] of Object.entries(cov)) {
            if (/\/(unit-tests|test)\//.test(f)) continue;       // product code only
            for (const k in e.s) { t++; if (e.s[k] > 0) h++; }
          }
          const report = fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'crap-all.txt'), 'utf8');
          const rows = report.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim().split(/\s+/)).filter((c) => c.length >= 5 && /\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(c[1]) && !/\/(unit-tests|test)\//.test(c[1]) && !isNaN(parseFloat(c[c.length - 1])));
          const scores = rows.map((c) => parseFloat(c[c.length - 1]));
          const max = Math.max(0, ...scores), over = scores.filter((x) => x > thr).length;
          const pct = t ? Math.round((1000 * h) / t) / 10 : 0;
          const colorMax = max <= 12 ? 'brightgreen' : max <= 30 ? 'yellow' : max <= 200 ? 'orange' : 'red';
          const colorOver = over === 0 ? 'brightgreen' : over <= 25 ? 'yellow' : over <= 150 ? 'orange' : 'red';
          const colorCov = pct >= 90 ? 'brightgreen' : pct >= 80 ? 'green' : pct >= 70 ? 'yellowgreen' : pct >= 50 ? 'yellow' : 'orange';
          const out = path.join(tmp, 'badges');
          fs.mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
          const w = (n, label, message, color) => fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, n), JSON.stringify({ schemaVersion: 1, label, message, color }) + '\n');
          w('crap-max.json', 'CRAP max', String(Math.round(max * 10) / 10), colorMax);
          w('crap-over.json', `CRAP > ${thr}`, `${over} fns`, colorOver);
          w('coverage.json', 'coverage', `${pct}%`, colorCov);
          console.log(`badges: max=${max} over=${over} coverage=${pct}%`);
          JS
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/badges"
          git init -q && git checkout -q -b badges
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'; git config user.email 'github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add -A && git commit -q -m "badges: main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          git push -q -f "https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" badges

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1063
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1063
- **Title**: gh-1061 Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1061` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +336
- **Deletions**: -24
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:38:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:52:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.
- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.
- `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` + `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`: added the AC5 sentence — ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md`, even when blocked; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

### Notes
- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

# Review State — Reviewer Verdict Context

What the reviewer decided on this PR and which threads are still open.
Decision values: `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (blocking — reviewer asked for changes), `APPROVED`, or `NONE` (no concluded review yet).

**Review decision: `NONE`**

No concluded review (CHANGES_REQUESTED/APPROVED) exists yet.

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.
- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.
- `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` + `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`: added the AC5 sentence — ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md`, even when blocked; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

### Notes
- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

The repo's CRAP threshold is 8 and the ratchet only allows pre-baseline offenders; every function introduced by this PR must land at ≤ 8. function shortThreadId(t) {
    var id = t.threadId ||
        (t.rootCommentId !== null && t.rootCommentId !== undefined ? 'comment#' + t.rootCommentId : 'no-id');
    id = String(id);
    return id.length > 16 ? id.substring(0, 13) + '...' : id;
}

function capLen(s, cap) {
    return s.length > cap ? s.substring(0, cap - 3) + '...' : s;
}

function threadShortLabel(t, maxLen) {
    if (!t) return '(unknown thread)';
    var body = String(t.body || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
    return capLen(shortThreadId(t) + (body ? ' — "' + body + '"' : ''), maxLen || 40);
}
```

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. }# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
