blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.
- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.
- `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` + `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`: added the AC5 sentence — ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md`, even when blocked; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

### Notes
- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

function capLen(s, cap) {

    var body = String(t.body || '').split('\n')[0].trim();

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \

- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.
- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

### Notes
- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1063
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1063
- **Title**: gh-1061 Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1061` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +336
- **Deletions**: -24
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:38:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:52:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. ## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]

## PR Description

Closes #1061
### Root Cause
- The blocked-rework PR comment inlined every unaddressed thread via `threadLabel()` before the agent's text, so on blocked passes the actionable message was buried (live: 39-thread dump on dmtools-dart PR #420) or silently absent when the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md`.
- The gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counted threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices), which can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable → the gh-395 week-long blocked loop.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: new `buildBlockedReworkComment` — ⚠️ header, then `outputs/response.md` verbatim, thread evidence moved into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", hard-capped labels via `threadShortLabel`, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence.
- `buildReplyCoverage` now splits open threads via `isUnaddressableThread` (`threadKeyOf() === null`); the gate denominator counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are reported as informational context in the fold.
- `runLapGate` feeds the addressable counts into `evaluateAuditResolveGate` (semantics for addressable threads unchanged) and passes the notice list to `handleReworkBlocked`.
- `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` + `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`: added the AC5 sentence — ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md`, even when blocked; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise.

### Test Coverage
- 12 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js`: comment composition (AC1/AC2/AC4), coverage denominator (UT-2/UT-4 + addressable-via-rootCommentId case), and action-level gate (UT-1 39-thread < 2000 chars, UT-2 all-null-id not blocked, UT-4/REG-1 mixed still blocks, AC4 placeholder).
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js`: 127 passed, 0 failed; full node harness: 5089 passed, 31 failed — the 31 failures are byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (unrelated harness/env issues).

### Notes
- A thread without `threadId` but with a `rootCommentId` remains addressable (replies can target it via `inReplyToId`) and stays in the denominator — only id-less threads are exempt.
- `handleReworkBlocked` now takes a 10th arg (`unaddressable`); all call sites updated (single caller: `runLapGate`).

function shortThreadId(t) {

function capLen(s, cap) {
    return s.length > cap ? s.substring(0, cap - 3) + '...' : s;
}

function threadShortLabel(t, maxLen) {
    if (!t) return '(unknown thread)';
    var body = String(t.body || '').split('\n')[0].trim();

}# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."
